title: Plant Scheduling Ruling: Keeping or Requoting the Production Slot After a Customer Hold — Factory Production Orders
content:
**Ruling.** For Factory Production Orders, how the ship date at a hold's release is first set depends on how long the hold ran, counted in calendar days from the hold start date to the release date, and on whether the order acknowledgment has been signed:

1. a hold of **at most 30 calendar days** on an order whose acknowledgment is signed keeps its production slot, so the current ship date is moved later by the business days of the hold, counted from the day after the hold start date up to and including the release date;
2. a hold **longer than 30 calendar days but within the class maximum hold length** on an order whose acknowledgment is signed is requoted from the release date by the business days of lead that remained when the hold began (counted from the day after the hold start date up to and including the current ship date) plus the class production queue days;
3. any other hold is requoted from the release date by the class standard lead time.

Business days are Monday through Friday, excluding U.S. federal holidays; in the first two cases the business days are counted forward starting the day after the date they are added to.

## Class figures used

| Build class | Maximum hold length (calendar days) | Production queue (business days) |
|---|---|---|
| Custom Size Build | 60 | 3 |
| Custom Color Build | 60 | 3 |
| Specialty Glass Build | 45 | 5 |
| Specialty Shape Build | 45 | 5 |
| Impact-Rated Build | 30 | 5 |
| Architectural Wood Build | 30 | 7 |

## Conditions in combination

| Hold length | Acknowledgment signed | Ship date first set |
|---|---|---|
| 30 calendar days or fewer | yes | current ship date moved later by the business days of the hold |
| 31 calendar days up to the class maximum | yes | release date plus remaining lead plus queue days |
| any length | no | release date plus class standard lead time |
| beyond the class maximum | yes | release date plus class standard lead time |

The signature is read from the acknowledgment signed checkpoint on the order's records; the current ship date is the one on the factory order record when the hold is released.

## Hypothetical cases (no federal holiday in the period)

- A Custom Size Build hold started on a Monday and is released on the Monday two weeks later (14 calendar days); the acknowledgment is signed. The hold spans 10 business days, so the current ship date moves 10 business days later.
- A Custom Color Build hold ran 40 calendar days; the acknowledgment is signed. At the hold start, 12 business days of lead remained to the current ship date. The ship date is first set 15 business days after the release date: 12 remaining and 3 queue days.
- An Impact-Rated Build hold of 20 calendar days on an order whose acknowledgment is not signed: the ship date is first set 50 business days after the release date.
